data.body:
ALL FIVE CRITERIA MET. Gerrit change 1104, LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1.

AC3 (code) — build_bedrock_provider now pre-checks boto3's own region resolution and raises a typed
LLMConfigError naming REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION. Asserted POSITIVELY (the error IS an LLMConfigError
and its message NAMES the setting), never as 'not a bare NoRegionError' — that negative form passes
vacuously, since any unrelated exception or a boto3 that stopped raising would satisfy it while
leaving the operator with the same unactionable failure. Two guard tests block the OPPOSITE
over-correction: an explicit rebar region still builds, and an ambient boto3 region is still
honoured, so an implementation that demanded rebar's knob unconditionally (breaking every developer
on AWS_REGION or a profile) cannot pass. Mutation-checked: disabling the pre-check fails exactly the
typed-error test. 30/30 bedrock tests; full suite 8182 passed / 0 failed.

AC1 + AC5 (runbook) — infra/runbooks/bedrock-access.md gains the measured evidence, the setting and
its value, and the IMDS-independence statement. It also gains a new 'how NOT to verify' entry,
because the runbook ENCODED THE BLIND SPOT: every probe in it passes --region explicitly, so none
ever exercised ambient resolution. That is precisely why NoRegionError survived an entire epic of
Bedrock verification.

AC2 [operator-attested] — the bot service environment, from inside compose-review-bot-1 AFTER the
change (docker exec ... env):

    AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1
    REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY=/opt/rebar/infra/compose/rebar-bot-signing-key
    REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION=us-east-1
    REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always
    REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets

AC4 [operator-attested] — boto3 with NO explicit region, from INSIDE the container, on the INSTANCE
ROLE (not an admin/wildcard identity):

    boto3 Session.region_name = us-east-1
    bedrock-runtime client   = OK, region: us-east-1
    converse (instance role) = ok

THE FINDING THIS SURFACED, and the reason AC4 was worth writing the way it was: setting ONLY
REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION was NOT sufficient. I set it, restarted the service, and boto3 STILL raised
NoRegionError — because that is rebar's OWN knob and boto3 has never heard of it. rebar's path worked
(it threads the value into BedrockProvider) while every other AWS caller in the image stayed
region-less. AC4's insistence on a BARE boto3 client with no explicit region is exactly what exposed
the conflation. Both vars are now set and they are NOT interchangeable:
  REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION -> rebar config layer + the signed verdict's provider_provenance (343b)
  AWS_DEFAULT_REGION       -> botocore's canonical var, every other caller

DURABILITY: /opt/rebar is a DEPLOYED COPY, not a git checkout, so the in-place edit alone would have
been reverted by the next deploy. The same change is in the repo at infra/compose/docker-compose.yml
and ships with change 1104. A backup of the deployed file is at docker-compose.yml.a574.bak and
'docker compose config' was validated before the container was recreated.
